subject: Agent-framework integration review — run against REAL installed SDKs (isolated venv) on ephemora-cell 1.2.0 core wheel
what_is_proven: LangGraph: a compiled StateGraph executed 4 real Ephemora Cell runs (3 lightweight tools SUCCESS, 1 heavy module correctly bounded by fuel).
LangChain: a real @tool (StructuredTool) invoked across 3 workloads (2 SUCCESS, 1 fuel-bounded) through the SDK wrapper.
CrewAI: the Ephemora Cell function is a real BaseTool registered on an Agent; invoking it through the framework executes WASM (SUCCESS).
OpenAI Agents: the Ephemora Cell function is a real FunctionTool bound to an Agent; the Cell-backed function it wraps executes WASM (SUCCESS).
what_is_NOT_exercised_here: The autonomous LLM decision loop (crew.kickoff() / Runner.run) — requires a model endpoint or OPENAI_API_KEY; deliberately NOT run (no unauthorized paid/ network LLM calls on this host). Both examples report llm_loop=skipped with the reason and still prove the tool-binding surface.

AutoGen and Semantic Kernel examples remain un-run here (their SDKs are heavier / Semantic Kernel is primarily .NET); they are documented as needing their own install and are not part of this evidence.
These are standalone scripts under integration/agent_frameworks/, NOT part of the CI pytest suite (testpaths=[tests]); running them does not change the collected test count.

crewai.llm_reason: OPENAI_API_KEY not set — crew.kickoff() requires an LLM provider

openai_agents.llm_reason: OPENAI_API_KEY not set — Runner.run() requires a model endpoint

honesty_note: Every SUCCESS above is a real WASM execution inside the Ephemora Cell sandbox driven through the named framework SDK installed in an isolated virtualenv; fuel_exhausted rows are the sandbox correctly enforcing a tight budget, not integration failures.
